title_en: Notes from the Sofa: A Cat's Diary
description_ru: Юмористический дневник высокомерного кота, который снисходительно наблюдает за странным поведением своих «домашних слуг».
text:
Monday. A day of no particular distinction, save that the staff failed, once again, to deliver breakfast at the proper hour. By proper, I mean five minutes before dawn. I made my feelings known through a series of discreet remarks on the bedroom carpet, a recital upon the wardrobe door and the careful, thoughtful removal of a glass of water from the bedside table, which I placed upon the floor, in order to see what would happen. What happened was that it fell. I am pleased to report that gravity continues to function. The Male Servant rose at last, muttering words that I do not recognise but that I suspect are a form of praise.

Having dined on a sachet of something described as "tuna medley," a dish that contains, as far as I can determine, no tuna and very little medley, I retired to the sofa, which I have long regarded as mine by right of conquest. It is a large, soft, tobacco-coloured object, and in the course of the afternoon I rotated upon it eleven times, a little the way a planet might, in the interest of finding the optimum angle of the sun. The staff tried to sit on it at six. I regarded them steadily until they remembered another engagement.

Tuesday. A distressing development. The Female Servant has returned from the outside world carrying a large and ominous object, which she calls a "suitcase", and which has the unmistakable smell of departure. I do not approve of departure. I took the precaution of lying in the suitcase at once, and nothing could persuade me to leave it, not even a handful of the expensive biscuits. She lifted me out, and I flowed back in, like a very reproachful liquid. In the end she went away with another bag entirely, a small and unimportant one, and I considered the matter settled.

Wednesday. Today I studied the large window, a rectangular portal which provides, at no charge, a continuous programme of nature documentary. There are birds, whom I regard as outrageous, and a squirrel, whom I regard as a personal enemy. I made the noise that I make for the birds, a sort of rapid chattering of the jaw, which the Male Servant finds endearing and which is, in fact, a declaration of intent. The glass is, of course, an unfair obstacle. I have been informed that this is a feature, not a flaw, of the system. I disagree, but I have decided to wait.

Thursday. At eleven this morning, the Male Servant produced a strange device that emits a red dot, and began to wave it about on the wall. I will admit, because I am an honest creature, that I was compelled to pursue it. It moved with great cunning and evaded me at every turn, and I flung myself at the skirting board, at the bookshelf and, in a moment I would prefer to forget, at the lamp. The Male Servant laughed uncontrollably. I wish it to be noted, for the record, that I was never truly deceived. I simply chose to humour him, as one does with a small, unintelligent god.

Friday. I had a visit from the Veterinarian, an individual who smells of antiseptic and betrayal. I was conveyed to the establishment in a plastic box, with all the dignity of a parcel, and subjected to a number of insulting indignities involving a thermometer. I would prefer not to elaborate. On the way home I maintained a stony silence, which they interpreted as sedation, and which was, in truth, a carefully calibrated sulk. As a reprisal, I have refused to use the new bed that was purchased for my comfort, and I have chosen instead to sleep in the box in which it arrived. This is the sort of thing the staff will never understand.

Saturday. A visitor arrived, a small human with sticky hands and a high voice, who was introduced to me as a "niece." She proceeded, with much enthusiasm, to pat me upon the head with the force of a person killing wasps. I endured it with great composure for nearly four seconds and then retreated beneath the dresser, where I remained, glaring, for most of the afternoon. At dusk, I emerged and nonchalantly knocked over her juice, in the interests of justice. Everyone shouted, except me.

Sunday. A day of rest, and a day of reflection. I have been giving some thought to the nature of my relationship with the staff, and I have reached certain conclusions. First, that they are, on the whole, a well-meaning and moderately useful species, if somewhat deficient in gratitude. Second, that they are intensely preoccupied with a small glowing rectangle, which they carry about with them and stare at throughout the day, and which they describe, absurdly, as "work." Third, that they possess an astonishing and misplaced confidence that I am theirs.

I have drafted a number of reforms. All meals shall henceforth be served on demand, at the moment of my choosing, which will be unpredictable. The sofa shall be reclassified as a sovereign territory. The vacuum cleaner, a screaming beast that the Female Servant pushes about with a smile, will be exiled to a shed. And the large cardboard boxes, which arrive at intervals in the hall, will be delivered in more generous quantities, since it is clear that a box is the finest creation of the human race, and the only one for which they deserve any real credit.

Monday, again. The cycle begins afresh. At five this morning, I surveyed the bedroom from the top of the wardrobe, and observed the two lumps of their bodies in the dark, breathing peacefully, with the trusting abandon of the truly defenceless. For a moment, I confess, I felt something approaching tenderness. It passed. I stepped delicately onto the Female Servant's face, to ensure that the day would begin in the correct order, and was rewarded, within minutes, with a bowl of tuna medley.

I took a small mouthful, pondered it and left the rest. One must maintain standards. But I sat nearby, and purred, a little, for just long enough to keep them guessing. After all, one does not wish them to become complacent. It is the first rule of management: keep your staff on their toes, and, if possible, on their knees, with a tin opener in their hand.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Лёгкий выдох без голоса, как дыхание на стекло; не произносите как русское «х», горло открыто.
Язык не касается нёба, губы слегка округлены; английское r не раскатывается.
Тёмный l: кончик языка упирается в дёсны, задняя часть оттянута назад; не смягчайте, как «ль».
Долгий округлый гласный: губы вытянуты вперёд, язык оттянут назад; не заменяйте на короткое «о».

questions.question: What did the cat knock off the bedside table?
Why did the cat lie in the suitcase?
questions.answer: To prevent the Female Servant from leaving.

questions.question: What does the cat say the small human visitor did?
questions.answer: She patted him roughly on the head, and he knocked over her juice.

questions.question: What does the cat do at the end to keep the staff guessing?
questions.answer: He leaves most of the tuna medley and purrs a little.
